It then has to be archived by hand." and the three numbered causes listed in the PR description (no `— resume.` block carries the stopped session's id; Zombie-checker cleanup only ran from resume hygiene; cleanup matched only `… — checker` / `… — waiting:` titles).
  expected_change_site: .claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md (and the workflow-templates twin), the Step 0 resume-hygiene / new "Issue-mode resume" placement so the cleanup actually fires after the plan is read; alternatively, an explicit Step 1 instruction to run the cleanup in issue mode.
  confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  EVIDENCE: No diff hunk places the issue-mode cleanup trigger in Step 1 (after "Read" in full), and no diff hunk revises the cleanup-section header to distinguish the issue-mode timing from the checker-cleanup "step 0" invariant. The new Step 0 bullet's text says "once step 1 has read the plan", but the bullet is delivered as a Step 0 child with no enforcement or contract test pinning the deferral. The stopping session therefore depends on the running session's interpretation of "once step 1 has read the plan" to actually fire the cleanup; an unattended session that attempts it as a Step 0 action falls through with no error, and the stopped session stays unarchived — re-introducing the hand-archive burden the PR is meant to remove.

  Why it fails at runtime: A session that walks Step 0's bullets in order, sees "once step 1 has read the plan" as a precondition predicate rather than a deferral directive, and attempts the cleanup before Step 1 reads the plan, will find no `Source issue:` line, never invoke `mcp__github__issue_read get_labels`, and quietly fall through — re-introducing the bug the PR is meant to fix (the stopped session stays unarchived).   File: .claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md
  Line or code reference: Step 0 bullet "Issue-mode resume without a `— resume.` block" (line 12)
  Problem: The bullet is positioned as a child of Step 0 (Session preflight), but the text explicitly states "once step 1 has read the plan, run the Zombie-checker cleanup too". The Zombie-checker cleanup section header (line 189) states "Every stage session runs this in step 0, after resume hygiene". The cleanup logic requires the source issue identifier from the plan header's `Source issue:` line, which is only available after Step 1 reads the plan.
  Why it fails at runtime: An unattended session following the literal step-by-step flow would attempt to run the cleanup at the end of Step 0, before Step 1 has read the plan. The source issue identifier would be unknown, the label check cannot run, and the stopped session would not be archived — exactly the failure mode this PR is meant to fix. The contract test `test_issue_mode_archives_stopped_stage_sessions` asserts the text exists but does not pin the bullet's placement relative to Step 1, so it does not catch this ordering contradiction.
  SEVERITY: BLOCKER
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
